legend: ✅ in the code · ⚠️ partial, or only on the provider side · ❌ none · 🔜 planned by the author, no code yet · — does not apply. Every cell was decided by reading the package as published on npm as of 2026-10-22, not its README; the column of @alexify/mailer is its plan for the channels as of 2026-11-07 (2.0 unless a release is named): its reliability layer is in the code for email (1.2), and takes the messages of the channels in 2.0.

groups.title: Runtimes (from imports and package metadata, not run)

sms.text: Twilio, Vonage, Infobip, Sinch, AWS End User Messaging

rcs.text: Google RBM, the SMS providers' RCS

push.text: FCM HTTP v1, APNs, Web Push
push.note: APNs requires HTTP/2, which Node’s `fetch` does not speak: it goes over `node:http2`. The tokens of FCM and APNs and the encryption of Web Push are `node:crypto`.

otherChannels.text: email: SMTP, sendmail, JMAP, 18 HTTP providers
otherChannels.note: Email is the channel of 1.x. LINE, WeChat, KakaoTalk, Zalo, Mattermost, Rocket.Chat or Matrix may follow 2.0, each when a user needs it; Signal and iMessage have no official API for this.

channelFallback.text: on refusal (2.1), or no receipt in time (2.2)
channelFallback.note: A message moves on when the provider refused it, when the recipient is not on the channel, or when no receipt says it was delivered within a deadline; never after a send of unknown outcome without an idempotency key. Email is one of the channels to fall back to.

templates.text: `./templates`: text by name, engines passed in

optOut.text: one list across channels and email (2.1)

deno.note: The 2.0.0 major release exists only to remove Deno as a supported runtime (CHANGELOG).

edge.note: Every SMS and chat provider and every webhook verifier uses only `fetch` and Web Crypto; APNs (`node:http2`) and the BullMQ / pg-boss / SQS queue adapters are Node-only.

sms.text: Twilio, Vonage, Plivo, MessageBird, Telnyx, SNS

rcs.note: Plain text sent through a Twilio Messaging Service that has an RCS sender may be upgraded to RCS on Twilio's side; nothing in the library knows about it.

whatsapp.note: No Cloud API provider and no template support; the Twilio receiver detects WhatsApp and `reply()` re-adds the `whatsapp:` prefix.

telegram.note: The provider sends text and `parse_mode` only: `blocks`, `threadId` and media are dropped. The receiver checks the secret token only when `secretToken` is set.

slack.note: Blocks and threads are sent; the Slack receiver verifies signatures and parses events, slash commands and interactions.

discord.text: incoming webhook only, plus interactions receiver
discord.note: No bot API, so no DMs; `blocks` become `embeds`. When a handler takes over 2 s the receiver defers the interaction, but `reply()` posts through the channel webhook, not as the interaction follow-up.

teams.note: Without `blocks` it posts a legacy `MessageCard`, the Office 365 connector format Microsoft is retiring; a Workflows webhook needs an Adaptive Card envelope you pass as `blocks`.

push.text: FCM HTTP v1, APNs, Web Push, Expo
push.note: FCM needs an OAuth access token you obtain yourself; APNs uses `node:http2` and `node:crypto` (Node-only) and targets the sandbox unless `production: true`. Web Push is VAPID + RFC 8291 on Web Crypto.

otherChannels.note: Email delegates to a `@visulima/email` instance; the in-app inbox has memory and unstorage stores.

providers.note: 6 SMS, 4 chat, 4 push, in-app, outbound webhook; plus `failover`, `roundrobin`, `opentelemetry` and `mock` wrappers.

failover.note: Tries the next provider on any failure (no error classification), each after its own HTTP retries.

channelFallback.note: Moves on only when a send fails: a suppressed or deduplicated send counts as success, and nothing waits for a delivery receipt.

retry.note: Each provider retries its POST 3 times on network errors, timeouts, 408/429 and 5xx (ignoring `Retry-After`); `retryMiddleware` and the queue worker retry again on top, and no idempotency key reaches the provider, so a timed-out SMS can go out more than once.

rateLimit.note: One bucket per `Notification`, shared by every channel and provider.

circuitBreaker.note: `circuitBreakerMiddleware` keeps a single state per instance, so failures of one SMS provider open it for push, chat and email too.

queue.note: The worker re-sends the whole message when any one channel fails; `UnstorageQueue` reservations never expire, so a crashed worker's job is stuck; `BullMqQueue` calls `getNextJob`, which a BullMQ `Queue` (as its docs say to pass) does not have.

media.note: Plivo advertises `media: true` but never sends `mediaUrls`; Telegram sends no media.

buttons.note: The Telegram provider drops `blocks`, so no inline keyboards; the Slack and Telegram receivers parse button callbacks.

templates.note: Liquid, Handlebars and ICU messages need optional peers; rendering is a separate step, not part of `send()`.

batch.note: A multi-recipient SMS counts as sent when any recipient succeeds, and the facade's receipt drops the per-recipient breakdown.

scheduled.note: No provider reads the payload's `scheduledAt`, though Twilio and Telnyx advertise `scheduling: true`; the SQS adapter caps delays at 15 minutes.

idempotency.note: The key never reaches a provider (despite its type doc), is not scoped per channel and is stored only after success, so after a partial failure a retry also skips the channel that failed.

receipts.text: one event type; only Twilio parses status
receipts.note: `NotificationEvent` (queued … read) is shared, but Standard Webhooks maps unknown types to `delivered`, the Slack and SNS parsers always return `delivered`, and nothing links events to sends.

webhookSignature.note: Twilio verification needs the public URL passed in; Telegram's secret token is optional.

optOut.text: suppression hook; the list is yours
optOut.note: A suppressed send is reported as `successful: true`, so `route()` stops there and does not try the next channel.

otel.note: Duck-typed: pass a tracer and meter; `@opentelemetry/api` is never imported.

auditLog.text: in-memory event store, fed by hand
auditLog.note: `NotificationEventBus` and `MemoryEventStore` exist, but the library never emits an event to them.

deps.note: bullmq, pg-boss, `@aws-sdk/client-sqs`, unstorage, liquidjs, handlebars, croner, intl-messageformat, `@opentelemetry/api`, `@visulima/email`, `@visulima/workflow`.

edge.note: The `Sms` and `Push` facades statically import the SNS, FCM and APNs connectors, which use Node's `crypto` and `Buffer`; the chat connectors use only `fetch`.

rcs.note: No RCS connector: Twilio Content API templates (`contentSid`, `contentVariables`) can go out as RCS when the Messaging Service has an RCS sender; the Infobip and Sinch connectors use SMS endpoints only.

slack.note: Incoming webhooks by design, with no Web API (`chat.postMessage`): `providerMessageId` is `null`.

teams.text: Workflows or legacy webhook, Adaptive Card
teams.note: Wraps the text in an Adaptive Card envelope and treats a legacy connector's HTTP 200 error body as a failure.

push.text: FCM v1, APNs, Expo, OneSignal, Beams, WonderPush
push.note: No VAPID Web Push of its own. APNs refuses to send without an HTTP/2-capable `fetch` you inject (Node's is HTTP/1.1) and needs a `tokenCache` in production.

otherChannels.note: 10 email providers: SES, Resend, Mailgun, SendGrid, Postmark, MailerSend, Mailtrap, Brevo, SparkPost, Scaleway.

providers.note: 10 SMS, 9 chat (WhatsApp and Telegram included), 6 push, 10 email; you can also pass a connector of your own.

buttons.text: Telegram keyboards, WhatsApp interactive, Slack blocks

receipts.note: `getMessageId` and `parseEventBody` from Novu are not implemented (MIGRATION.md).

webhooks.note: Twilio `statusCallback`, Infobip `notifyUrl`, Telnyx `webhookUrl`, Sinch `callbackUrl` are passed through.

maintainer.note: The README lists the Vonage id as `nexmo`, but only `vonage` is accepted; MIGRATION.md says the alias was removed in 1.0.

edge.text: Hono/h3 adapters, but imports Node built-ins
edge.note: The main entry statically imports `path`, `process`, `url` and `async_hooks` and reads `process.env` and `process.hrtime`, so a Worker needs `nodejs_compat`. Nothing in the package declares edge support. Sending itself runs on the Novu server.

sms.text: 38 SMS provider ids, on Novu server

whatsapp.note: The `whatsapp-business` provider posts to `graph.facebook.com` (Meta's official API). Novu agents can also reply on WhatsApp.

telegram.note: The `telegram` id is in `@novu/shared` 2.10.0 and in the framework's provider schemas. The last `@novu/providers` on npm (2.6.6, Feb 2025) has no Telegram code, so the sending code ships only inside the Novu server.

slack.note: In `@novu/providers` 2.6.6, `slack` posts to the subscriber's incoming `webhookUrl`. `@novu/shared` 2.10.0 adds `slack_channel`/`slack_user` endpoints and a signing secret, and Slack is also an agent platform for inbound messages.

discord.text: `discord`: incoming webhook, on the Novu server
discord.note: Discord as an agent platform (inbound) is marked `comingSoon` in `@novu/shared`.

teams.text: `msteams`: Azure Bot, on the Novu server
teams.note: In `@novu/providers` 2.6.6, `msteams` posts to an incoming `webhookUrl`. `@novu/shared` 2.10.0 asks for a Microsoft App ID, client secret and tenant ID (Azure Bot / Bot Framework) and adds `ms_teams_channel`/`ms_teams_user` endpoints.

googleChat.note: The framework's provider override schemas already have a `google-chat` key, but the integration catalog in `@novu/shared` 2.10.0 has no Google Chat provider. It appears only in the list of coming-soon agent platforms.

push.note: The ids `pusher-beams`, `appio` and `push-webhook` also exist. Web Push works only through FCM's `webPush` override, Pushpad or OneSignal; no provider sends VAPID Web Push directly.

otherChannels.text: email, in-app, LINE, iMessage, Webex, Mattermost, Zulip…
otherChannels.note: Also Rocket.Chat, Ryver, GetStream, Grafana OnCall, a generic chat webhook, and tool steps (PagerDuty, Opsgenie, webhook). There is no voice channel.

providers.note: Counted in `@novu/shared` 2.10.0 `types/providers.js`: 23 email, 38 SMS, 16 chat, 8 push and 1 in-app. These include Novu's own demo and webhook providers. `@novu/providers` 2.6.6, the last version on npm, has 66 implementations.

failover.note: An integration has `primary`, `priority` and `conditions` fields. The published packages show no retry on another provider after an error.

channelFallback.note: Only the in-app step returns a result (`seen`, `read`). The SMS, chat, email and push result schemas are empty, so a step cannot react to an SMS or WhatsApp delivery failure.

retry.note: The package never retries a trigger. Retries happen in the server's job runner (the execution-details model in `@novu/shared` has an `isRetry` field).

rateLimit.text: throttle step, on the Novu server

timeout.text: trigger `fetch` has no timeout or signal

queue.text: jobs persisted on the Novu server

media.text: chat card images, agent file replies
media.note: The SMS step has `body` only and the email step has no attachments field.

waTemplates.note: In `@novu/providers` 2.6.6, `whatsapp-business` sends a template only when it receives `customData.template`. The framework has no model for WhatsApp templates.

scheduled.text: delay steps (cron, date), on the Novu server

idempotency.note: The package sends `transactionId` and uses it to cancel a trigger. The package does not show whether the server rejects a duplicate.

receipts.note: `@novu/shared` defines events such as `message.sent`, `message.delivered`, `message.failed` and `message.read` for Novu's outbound webhooks.

webhooks.text: 13 providers parsed, on the Novu server
webhooks.note: In `@novu/providers` 2.6.6, `parseEventBody` exists for 8 email providers and 5 SMS providers (Twilio, Plivo, Telnyx, Termii, RingCentral).

webhookSignature.note: The bridge checks a `novu-signature` HMAC with a 5-minute window, but only when `NODE_ENV` is set to something other than `development`/`dev`, or when `strictAuthentication` is on. The provider code verifies no signatures on status webhooks.

inbound.note: The conversational providers are Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp Business, MS Teams, Sendblue and Novu email (`@novu/shared` `conversational-providers.js`).

optOut.text: subscriber preferences, on the Novu server

quietHours.text: preferences and weekly schedule, on the Novu server

auditLog.text: activity feed, on the Novu server

deps.note: There are also 13 optional peer dependencies (express, next, hono, zod, ai, langchain…).

messenger.text: listed as a TODO in the source

telegram.text: listed as a TODO in the source

push.text: APNs, Web Push (VAPID), WNS, ADM; FCM broken
push.note: From reading the code, not running it: the `fcm` provider passes its config as `gcm` settings (`lib/providers/push/fcm.js`). node-pushnotifications 3.1.1 sends Android tokens through its FCM v1 path, which reads `fcm` settings that are never set, and its `gcm` path uses Google's legacy API, shut down in 2024.

providers.note: 7 email, 9 SMS, 4 push, and 1 each for voice (Twilio), web push, Slack and WhatsApp.

channelFallback.note: `send()` sends every channel in the request at once with `Promise.all`. Nothing falls back from one channel to another.

retry.text: moves to the next provider, no backoff

queue.note: `notifme-sdk-queue-rabbitmq` 4.0.0 was last published in 2017 and gets ~9 downloads a week.

mock.note: A channel with no providers configured silently falls back to the logger provider. It logs the whole request (recipient included) to the console and reports success with a random id.

retry.note: The core retries only `getMe`, `deleteWebhook` (when polling starts) and `getUpdates`, never a send. The plugin's defaults are unlimited attempts and unlimited wait, and it also retries network errors, so a lost response can send a message twice.

webhookSignature.note: The check is optional: when no `secretToken` is set, `webhookCallback` accepts every request. Telegram sends a shared secret header and does not sign payloads.

moduleFormat.text: CJS for Node, ESM web bundle

retry.note: Two retries by default, on every method. A timed-out `sendMessage` is sent again, so a lost response can send a message twice.

rateLimit.text: opt-in token bucket, global and per chat

webhookSignature.note: `webhookCallback` throws at setup unless you set `secretToken` or pass `allowUnauthenticated: true`. The comparison runs in constant time.

inbound.text: long polling and a web-standard webhook

hooks.note: The only way to hook outgoing API calls is to inject your own `fetch`.

types.text: built in, generated from Bot API docs

downloads.note: Most downloads are of 0.66/0.67. Version 2.1.0 gets ~8.7k a week (npm per-version API).

maintainer.note: Version 1.0.0 came out on 2026-06-12 and 2.0.0 on 2026-08-16. The README says v2 is a from-scratch redesign with no v1 compatibility.

edge.note: `lib/base/RequestClient.js` builds an `https.Agent` for axios and reads `fs`; `lib/webhooks/webhooks.js` uses Node `crypto`.

messenger.note: Notify's Facebook Messenger option (`facebookMessengerPageId`) is marked Deprecated in `lib/rest/notify/v1/service.d.ts`; Conversations is the remaining path.

push.note: No Web Push. The package does not mark Notify itself deprecated, only its Messenger and Alexa options; Conversations has separate APN/FCM credentials for its own client SDKs.

otherChannels.text: MMS, voice, video, email, in-app chat, Apple Messages
otherChannels.note: Conversations still lists `gbm` (Google Business Messages), a channel Google shut down in 2024.

retry.note: Full-jitter exponential backoff, 3 retries by default; 5xx and network errors are never retried, and `maxRetries: 0` silently becomes 3 because of `||` (`lib/base/RequestClient.js`).

idempotency.note: Only a few other APIs (Conversations v2, call Payments, user-defined messages) accept an idempotency key.

webhookSignature.note: Timing-safe compare, tries the URL with and without port, and `validateRequestWithBody` checks `bodySHA256` for JSON bodies (`lib/webhooks/webhooks.js`). The scheme has no timestamp, so replays are not rejected.

mock.note: Twilio test credentials work on the provider side; a custom `httpClient` can stub requests.

nodeMin.note: No `engines` field; the bundled README lists Node.js 20 LTS or later.

edge.text: Workers, Vercel Edge declared; fetch only

browser.note: There is no `dangerouslyAllowBrowser`-style check, so client-side use ships the API key.

teams.note: The Teams resources (Operator Connect, direct routing, meeting bots) are telephony, not Teams messaging.

push.note: `mobilePushCredentials` (iOS/Android) only attach to SIP connections so Telnyx can wake its own calling SDK; there is no API to send push notifications.

otherChannels.text: MMS, voice, video rooms, fax, email

retry.note: Retries 408/409/429/5xx and timeouts, message POSTs included, but adds no idempotency key by itself; pass `Idempotency-Key` to avoid duplicate sends (`client.js`).

webhooks.note: `JSON.parse` plus a TypeScript cast, with no runtime schema check (`lib/webhooks.js`).

deps.note: `ws` is needed only for the speech WebSocket helpers.

maintainer.note: Ships several releases a month (7.25 → 7.28 between 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-22).

deno.note: package.json maps a long list of runtime conditions (deno, bun, workerd, …) to the same build; the README only mentions Node.js.

edge.note: `@vonage/auth` imports Node `fs` and `crypto` at load, JWTs use `jsonwebtoken`, and `@vonage/server-client` reads `process.version` on every request.

rcs.note: The bundled `@vonage/messages` README lists RCS as Beta.

channelFallback.note: `MessageWithFailover` passes a `failover` list of channel messages to the Messages API; the SDK does not act on it.

timeout.note: `@vonage/server-client` uses an AbortController only when `timeout` is set; callers cannot pass their own AbortSignal.

buttons.text: RCS suggestions, Viber button, WA custom

webhooks.text: SMS DLR type only; no parser

webhookSignature.note: `@vonage/jwt` `verifySignature` checks the JWT but not its `payload_hash` against the body and is not re-exported by `@vonage/server-sdk`; SMS `verifySignature` compares with `===`, not timing-safe.

retry.note: Only voice API calls are retried: twice on 5xx, immediately, without backoff (`dist/rest/axios.js`).

batch.note: Bulk is done by the provider: the SDK only joins an array `dst` into Plivo's `<`-delimited form (`dist/resources/messages.js`).

webhookSignature.note: Compares with `===` (not timing-safe) and does not track nonces against replay (`dist/utils/v3Security.js`).

mock.note: `dist/rest/client-test.js` is the SDK's own fixture client with hard-coded responses, not a documented test mode.

deps.note: `request` backs only the bundled test client; runtime deps also include `@types/node@14` and the `querystring` shim. Importing the client overwrites the global `axios.defaults.httpAgent`/`httpsAgent` (`dist/rest/axios.js`).

otherChannels.text: MMS, LINE, WeChat, KakaoTalk, Apple, voice, fax
otherChannels.note: Apple Messages for Business is the Conversation channel `APPLEBC`; verification is in `@sinch/verification`.

retry.note: On by default (3 retries, configurable `retryPolicy`); 5xx and network errors are not retried (`@sinch/sdk-client/dist/client/retry-policy.js`).

receipts.note: Conversation delivery events share one model across its channels; SMS delivery reports are a separate model.

webhookSignature.note: `validateWebhookSignature` compares with `===` (not timing-safe), never checks the timestamp's age, and re-serializes object bodies with `JSON.stringify` (`@sinch/sdk-client/dist/utils/authorization.helper.js`).

deps.note: Sub-packages bring `node-fetch@2.7.0` and `form-data`; `@sinch/sdk-client` requires `@sinch/sdk-core/package.json` without declaring it.
